sections.heading: Texas deadline overview
paragraphs: Most Texas car accident injury lawsuits must be filed within 2 years of the injury date. Missing this deadline can permanently bar recovery.
Wrongful death, government-entity, and minor claimant cases may follow different rules. This article is educational — confirm your dates with a licensed Texas attorney.

sections.heading: Why waiting hurts Fort Worth claims
paragraphs: With ~26,237 annual crashes in the Fort Worth area, evidence fades fast: skid marks wash away, witnesses relocate, and video is overwritten.
Insurers begin building a file immediately. Early recorded statements can lock in descriptions before you know the full extent of injuries.

sections.heading: Comparative fault in Texas
paragraphs: Texas follows 51% bar rules. If you are found partially at fault, compensation may be reduced or barred depending on your percentage.
Document everything that supports the other driver's negligence — traffic citations, 911 calls, and witness statements.

sections.heading: Insurance minimums and coverage gaps
paragraphs: Texas requires at least 30/60/25 in liability coverage (verify current law). Many at-fault drivers carry only minimums.
Review your declarations page for UM/UIM, MedPay, and PIP. These coverages can matter when the other driver is uninsured or underinsured in Fort Worth.

sections.heading: Government and special entities
paragraphs: Claims involving city buses, state vehicles, or federal property often require earlier notice than the standard 2-year window. Missing a notice deadline can defeat an otherwise valid claim.

paragraphs: Day 1–7: Medical care, police report, insurer notification (facts only).
Week 2–8: Follow treatment plans, gather bills, avoid social media posts about the crash.
Month 2+: If injuries continue, consult counsel before accepting settlement releases.

sections.heading: Texas fault and comparative negligence
paragraphs: Texas follows modified comparative negligence with a 51% bar. If you are more than 50% at fault, you may recover nothing. Insurers in Fort Worth routinely argue shared fault to reduce payouts—your documentation from day one shapes that fight.

Police reports, witness statements, traffic citations, and scene photos help establish who failed to yield, follow speed limits, or maintain a safe distance. Never admit fault at the scene; describe facts calmly to officers.
list: Request the responding officer's name and report number
Note weather, lighting, and road conditions
Identify surveillance cameras at nearby businesses
Save dashcam or phone video immediately

sections.heading: Fort Worth insurance minimums and coverage gaps
paragraphs: Texas requires minimum liability limits of 30/60/25 ($30,000 per person bodily injury, $60,000 per accident, $25,000 property damage). Many at-fault drivers carry only minimums—often insufficient for hospital bills after a serious Fort Worth collision.

Review your declarations page for uninsured/underinsured motorist (UM/UIM), personal injury protection (PIP), and MedPay. These coverages can matter when the other driver has inadequate limits or flees the scene.

sections.heading: Medical treatment and documentation
paragraphs: Insurers scrutinize gaps in treatment. After a Fort Worth crash, seek care within 24 hours even if pain feels minor—whiplash, concussion, and internal bleeding may appear later. ER records, urgent care notes, and follow-up visits create a timeline insurers cannot easily dismiss.

Keep itemized bills, imaging orders (X-ray, MRI, CT), prescriptions, physical therapy schedules, and mileage to appointments. Bobby Garcia Law's medical specialists help clients organize treatment records for maximum clarity.

sections.heading: Dealing with claims adjusters
paragraphs: Adjusters represent the insurance company's financial interests—not yours. They may request recorded statements, broad medical releases, or quick settlements before you understand injury severity. In Fort Worth and across Texas, early statements can lock in descriptions that reduce fault on the other driver.

Provide basic facts—date, time, location, vehicles involved. Decline recorded interviews until you understand coverage and injuries. Request denials, reservation-of-rights letters, and settlement offers in writing.

sections.heading: Evidence preservation in the first 30 days
paragraphs: Skid marks fade, witnesses forget details, and business surveillance video is often deleted within 7–30 days. After a crash on Fort Worth highways or surface streets, send preservation letters to businesses, municipalities, and trucking companies when commercial vehicles are involved.

Preserve repair estimates, rental receipts, tow bills, and cell-phone metadata. Social media posts about the crash or your activities can be used against you—avoid discussing fault or activities online.

sections.heading: Commercial trucks and 18-wheelers
paragraphs: Fort Worth corridors see heavy commercial traffic. Trucking cases involve federal motor carrier rules, electronic logging devices, black-box data, and multiple defendants (driver, carrier, broker, shipper). Evidence spoils quickly—qualified counsel helps preserve downloads and driver qualification files.

sections.heading: Statute of limitations and notice deadlines
paragraphs: Most Texas personal injury claims must be filed within two years of the injury date. Government-entity cases (city buses, state vehicles) may require earlier notice—sometimes within months. Missing a deadline can permanently bar recovery regardless of merit.
Calendar your dates immediately after a Fort Worth crash. Bobby Garcia Law offers free consultations 24/7 at (956) 668-7400 to help you understand timelines—Justice Made Simple.

sections.heading: Property damage and total-loss disputes
paragraphs: Insurers may undervalue repairs or declare a total loss based on comparables that favor the carrier. Obtain independent estimates from reputable body shops in Fort Worth. Review valuation reports for missing equipment, recent maintenance, and regional price adjustments.

sections.heading: Lost wages and economic damages
paragraphs: Document every missed shift, PTO day, and reduced earning capacity. Employers in Fort Worth can provide verification letters; self-employed victims should gather tax returns, contracts, and invoices showing lost opportunities. Vocational experts may be needed for long-term disability.

sections.heading: Pain, suffering, and non-economic damages
paragraphs: Texas allows recovery for physical pain, mental anguish, disfigurement, and loss of enjoyment of life when liability and causation are established. Journals documenting sleep loss, anxiety, and daily limitations can support these elements—start early after your Fort Worth collision.

sections.heading: Settlement vs. litigation timeline
paragraphs: Minor property claims may resolve in weeks; injury claims with treatment, disputed fault, or commercial defendants often take months or years. Mediation, discovery, and expert depositions extend timelines but may increase recovery. Never sign a general release while treatment is ongoing.
